what: The ranges::to sidebar gets the GCC version history wrong. std::ranges::to itself is complete in GCC 14's library. Only the rest of P1206R7 (the containers' from_range constructors and insert_range/append_range members) arrived in GCC 15. The lab repeats the error by pointing readers to GCC 15.
evidence: Page P37: "It's in GCC's library from version 14 (partly) and 15 (fully)." Lab 4: "lets you switch to GCC 15 to try std::ranges::to for real". GCC commit r14-5794 "libstdc++: Define std::ranges::to for C++23 (P1206R7)" (https://gcc.gnu.org/pipermail/libstdc++-cvs/2023q4/040666.html): "This adds the std::ranges::to functions for C++23 ... The rest of P1206R7 is not yet implemented, i.e. the new constructors taking the std::from_range tag, and the new insert_range, assign_range, etc. member functions." Container-adaptor from_range members came in r15-8039 (https://gcc.gnu.org/pipermail/libstdc++-cvs/2025q1/042703.html).
fix: P37: "It's in GCC's library from version 14." Lab: "switch to GCC 14 or newer". If wanted, add: "(the matching container constructors arrived in GCC 15)".

what: The invalidation table leaves out the end() bookmark. Erasing the last element of a deque also invalidates end(), and any vector or deque insertion invalidates end(). The table says 'only the erased one'.
evidence: P23: "deque | ... | at either end: only the erased one". The standard ([deque.modifiers]) says: "An erase operation that erases the last element of a deque invalidates only the past-the-end iterator and all iterators and references to the erased elements."
fix: Add the end bookmark to the table: deque erase "at either end: the erased one (and end())"; vector erase "the erased one, everything after it, and end()". Or add a footnote: "end() is always invalidated by inserting or erasing in a vector or deque".
